items.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024
items.q: my stint with Abdullah Ibrahim, I played with him five years

ctx.x: I’ll give you several, that’s fine.

Okay. Well my stint with Abdullah Ibrahim, I played with him five years, enjoyed his music, learned a lot from him. That was the longest stint I’ve ever been with any particular band or situation. Then the best band leader that I work with and I always say stands out in my mind, Marvin Gaye, because of what he did after the gig. He would come down after all of the accolades and women being you know flirtatious and throwing their underwear on the bandstand. He would come down every night, look me in my eyes, shake…

friend, like what we consider myself as a brother — because I never had a brother — Freddy Waite, we were in the first grade together and throughout college and everything it was a very strong influence. He was responsible for me getting in the band and doing a lot of things. But Marvin and I we used to talk about Freddy, how Freddy helped him play, you know taught him drums. Because Marvin could play the piano, he’d play the drums, he’d play several other instruments. So that one of the highlights of my life.…
